scenarios.title: apply_discount_premium_and_regular
scenarios.rationale: Verify that the discount logic applies a 10% reduction for premium customers and leaves other customers unchanged, including edge cases of zero and negative totals.
scenarios.assumptions: apply_discount returns total * 0.90 for customer_type == "premium"; no validation of total sign; function is pure and deterministic.

scenarios.title: checkout_integration_with_calculate_total_and_discount
scenarios.rationale: Ensure checkout correctly composes calculate_total and apply_discount, handling typical, large, and floating‑point inputs.
scenarios.assumptions: checkout calls calculate_total(price, quantity) then apply_discount on the result; price and quantity are numeric (int or float); discount rules are as defined in apply_discount.

scenarios.title: calculate_refund_uses_apply_discount
scenarios.rationale: Validate that refunds.calculate_refund mirrors the discount logic from billing.apply_discount, confirming the direct dependency after the change.
scenarios.assumptions: calculate_refund simply forwards its arguments to apply_discount; no additional logic is added; customer_type handling is identical to apply_discount.

scenarios.title: generate_sales_report_reflects_checkout_output
scenarios.rationale: Confirm that reports.generate_sales_report returns a dictionary with the correct total_sales value derived from checkout, covering premium and regular customers.
scenarios.assumptions: generate_sales_report calls checkout internally; the returned dict always contains the key "total_sales"; no error handling for invalid inputs is present.
